title: Red de Senderos de la Sierra Blanca
summary: The partial document covers the annual report for the "Red de Senderos de la Sierra Blanca" for the year 2025. It includes sections on the presentation of the network, budget and financial statements, environmental volunteerism, route safety, biodiversity, and collaborations.

title: Presentación de la red
summary:
The main points covered in the partial document are:
- The red of senderos (trails) in Sierra Blanca includes 412 kilometers of signposted routes distributed across 27 homologated routes.
- Maintenance is managed by the consortium since 2004.
- Routes are classified into 8 major circuits over 20 kilometers, 12 medium traverses, and 7 local trails.
- The most frequented route is the ascent to Pico Almirante.

title: Presupuesto y cuentas
summary: The partial document covers the budget and accounts related to the marking and signage of paths. It mentions that the 2025 expenditure for marking and signage was funded from the conservation line and not from the current accounts. The document details that 1,240 wooden panels were repainted and 380 stone markers were placed on crest paths during 2025. Additionally, the review of the signage covered 178 kilometers of paths.

title: Voluntariado ambiental
summary: The partial document covers the economic aspects of hiking in a specific comarca (region). It includes data from surveys of hikers and agreements with lodging establishments, such as 45 refugios and rural houses under the Sendero Amigo card. The average expenditure of a hiker was found to be 31 euros per day based on the 2025 survey.

title: Seguridad en rutas
summary: The partial document covers safety on routes, mentioning rescue team interventions for non-fatal incidents such as sprains and dehydration, mostly occurring in July and August. It also mentions the mapping of 60 kilometers of exposed route segments using drones and the annual analysis of the Fuente del Roble, which was found to be potable in all samples.

title: Biodiversidad
summary: The partial document covers the biodiversity in an area, mentioning a census of the Pyrenean sheep, which has a slight expansion towards the Frío river valley. It also notes that there are 9 breeding pairs of the royal eagle. Additionally, it highlights the largest population of mountain juniper in the region's peaks and mentions that botanical monitoring plots are measured twice a year at 26 fixed points.

title: Colaboraciones
summary: The partial document covers collaborations within a consortium of 12 municipalities that work with a regional university to track fauna. It mentions an mobile app with over 38,000 downloads, three active tourism companies operating under annual authorization, and a partnership with Valdemoros neighborhood association to restore an old cobblestone path.
